## Reusable prerequisite: higher-order differentiation under the integral sign

## Reusable prerequisite: Hardy–Littlewood maximal theorem for a homogeneous gauge

Justification: the 2-tree case of the tree estimate (§7.2, texline~716–760) needs Lemma 7.2 (radially decreasing
majorants are controlled by the maximal function) and the `L²` bound for the anisotropic maximal function
(texline~755–758). Mathlib has no maximal function and no Hardy–Littlewood theorem, only the abstract Vitali covering
lemma. The Hardy–Littlewood maximal theorem and the control of approximate identities are standard textbook results
(Stein 1993, Ch. I; Grafakos, Classical Fourier Analysis, §2.1). Formulated for a translation-invariant (and, for the
majorization, reflection-invariant) measure on a topological group with a continuous, symmetric, subadditive gauge
`ρ`, `ρ(0) = 0`, whose balls scale like `r^D`. File `CarlesonLT/Auto/HardyLittlewoodMaximal.lean`.
